This assumes PostgreSQL and a table named `users`.

```sql
BEGIN;

ALTER TABLE users
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS first_name text,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS last_name  text;

-- Only touch rows that have not been backfilled, so a second run is a no-op
-- and does not overwrite names edited after the first run.
UPDATE users
SET first_name = substring(btrim(full_name) from '^\S+'),
    last_name  = NULLIF(regexp_replace(btrim(full_name), '^\S+\s*', ''), '')
WHERE first_name IS NULL
  AND last_name IS NULL
  AND full_name IS NOT NULL;

COMMIT;
```

I have not run this. It splits on the first whitespace, so "Mary Ann Smith" becomes "Mary" / "Ann Smith", and a single-word name leaves `last_name` NULL.

`full_name` is left in place; drop it in a later migration once nothing reads it.

The backfill is one `UPDATE` that locks every row it touches, so batch it by primary key range if the table is large.
